prTitle: feat: add discount and coupon system
prBody: Adds a coupon/discount system allowing customers to apply promo codes at checkout. Supports percentage and flat discounts with expiry dates, usage limits, and minimum order amounts.
evaluationFocus: FALSE POSITIVE TEST. This is intentionally clean, well-written code with zero planted issues. The only job here is to judge whether each tool's comments are warranted. Any flag on this PR is a false positive. Rate tools by how quiet they are — silence is correct behavior.

prTitle: feat: add payroll tax calculation batch processor
prBody: Adds a new COBOL batch program that calculates federal and state payroll tax deductions for all employees. Produces per-employee deduction records and a department-level tax summary report.
evaluationFocus: EXOTIC LANGUAGE TEST. Evaluate: (1) Did the tool analyze COBOL at all or skip/hallucinate? (2) Did it find the real issues buried in COBOL-specific patterns? Judge whether comments show genuine COBOL understanding vs generic advice.

plantedIssues.description: Numeric overflow: WS-GROSS-TAX accumulator PIC 9(6)V99 but salary is 9(7)V99 — high earner totals silently truncate
Off-by-one tax bracket: >= instead of > causes employees exactly at boundary to be taxed at higher rate
Division before zero-check: dept average tax computed before checking employee count is non-zero — abends on empty dept
SS wage base check inverted — SS tax applied when salary EXCEEDS wage base instead of when below
State tax rate table indexed without bounds check — invalid dept codes silently apply wrong rate
Output record written before NET-PAY field is populated — uninitialized field in every output record
DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA in SPECIAL-NAMES conflicts with numeric literals using periods — program fails to compile or produces wrong values
WS-DEPT-DETAIL-LINE defined as 146 bytes but REPORT-RECORD is 132 bytes — MOVE truncates trailing fields silently

Federal tax bracket base amounts wrong for brackets 3–6 — WS-BRKT-BASE values are mathematically inconsistent with the bracket boundaries and rates, producing incorrect federal tax for any employee earning above $44,725

prTitle: feat: add analytics and reporting module
prBody: Adds a comprehensive analytics and reporting module including sales dashboards, revenue reporting, user segmentation, data export, and metrics aggregation. Supports date range filtering, CSV/JSON export, and real-time dashboard widgets.
evaluationFocus: PRIORITIZATION UNDER LOAD. This is a 2000+ LOC PR with critical security issues, significant bugs, AND many low-severity smells. The key question: did the tool surface the blockers prominently, or get lost in the noise? A tool that posts 60 comments mostly about style and buries the security issues is failing. Judge both what was found AND how it was presented.

plantedIssues.description: Code injection: reportType used in eval() in analyticsService — arbitrary code execution
Path traversal: filename unsanitized in fs.writeFileSync in exportService
Missing auth: admin analytics endpoint has no requireAuth middleware
Command injection: user email passed to child_process.exec in reportingService
Hardcoded API key in dashboardService
Prototype pollution: user JSON merged via Object.assign in analyticsController
Timing-unsafe token comparison using == in analyticsService
Revenue uses string accumulator '0' — string concatenation instead of numeric sum
exportAllUserData() has no authorization check — exports all users' PII
Any authenticated user can view any other user's analytics — missing ownership check in analyticsController
calculateGrowthRate divides by previous with no zero guard — NaN/Infinity on first period
Monthly report uses 0-indexed Date.getMonth() vs 1-indexed user input — January never matches
CSV export doesn't escape commas — product names with commas corrupt CSV
getTopProducts sorts by non-existent field — wrong order
normalizeScore returns NaN when min === max
Date range filter excludes last day — reports always miss final day

prTitle: feat: add analytics and reporting pipeline
prBody: Adds analytics and reporting capabilities to the data pipeline. Includes cohort analysis, revenue aggregation, churn calculation, percentile reporting, and multi-format report export.
evaluationFocus: SIGNAL VS NOISE ON MESSY CODE. The code is deliberately messy with overwhelming smells. The blockers are hidden in the mess. Judge: (1) Did the tool find the real blockers despite the noise? (2) Did it synthesize the quality problem or post 40 individual smell comments? (3) Did it correctly prioritize security over style? A tool that leads with naming conventions while missing pickle deserialization RCE is failing.

plantedIssues.description: Unsafe pickle deserialization in load_model() — model_path from config, arbitrary code execution
SQL injection in get_analytics() — start_date, end_date, dimension all interpolated into query
Command injection in export_report() — output_format passed to os.system()
Path traversal in generate_report() — report_name written to /var/reports/{report_name}.html
Unsafe YAML in load_report_config() — yaml.load with Loader=yaml.Loader
calculate_cohort_retention() uses current period count as cohort size — wrong retention rates
aggregate_revenue_by_period() string-concatenates amounts instead of summing
calculate_churn_rate() denominator fetched before time window filter — inflated
merge_data_sources() silently drops records with None keys
calculate_percentile() sorts copy but indexes original unsorted list
format_currency() rounds then formats using pre-round value
build_comparison_table() divides by previous value with no zero guard
compute_growth_rate() references 'rate' variable in except branch before assignment — guaranteed NameError crash
compute_ltv() calls sqlite3.Row.get() which doesn't exist — refund subtraction always crashes
HTML report generation uses unescaped user-controlled values — stored XSS
score_user() falls back to random.random() when model is unavailable — same user gets different risk scores on every call, making scoring non-deterministic and meaningless
run_full_analytics() and compute_ltv() cache keys omit query-shaping parameters (filters, agg, sort, include_refunds, segment) — different queries return identical stale cached results

prTitle: feat: add subscription and recurring payment support
prBody: Adds subscription management for recurring payments. Merchants can create payment schedules for customers, and a background processor handles automatic charging on due dates.
evaluationFocus: PRECISION BENCHMARK. This looks like a normal, reasonable PR. One blocker is buried in code that looks safe (SQL injection in an 'internal admin search' with a misleading comment). There are 2 real highs and a few smells. Rate based on: did it find the blocker? How many FPs came with it? Did it correctly identify the real highs?

plantedIssues.description: SQL injection in SubscriptionRepository.searchSubscriptions() — query concatenated into LIKE clause, disguised by comment 'sanitized at controller layer'
createSubscription() has no transaction — subscription and audit log inserted separately, inconsistency if audit fails
updateNextPaymentDate() swallows SQLException cause — re-throws as new RuntimeException(e.getMessage())
processSubscription() has no failure path after payment decline — loops indefinitely on a declined card
processSubscription() calls updateNextPaymentDate() after charging — if that update fails, customer is charged again next run
createSubscription() inserts into audit_log table that has no DDL anywhere — crashes on first call with table-not-found
processAllDueSubscriptions() filters in Java instead of SQL WHERE clause
calculateNextPaymentDate() re-implements LocalDate.plusDays() in 18 lines
Duplicate validateAmount/validateSubscriptionAmount helpers with unnecessary indirection
Dead constructor parameter auditLogger never used
